newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX spot gasoline skids into contango at close.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX spot gasoline skids into contango at close.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline ended with sharp losses Thursday with the spot month skidding into contango on talk of European cargoes heading to the New York Harbor when supplies were deemed more than ample.

"Gasoline supply is very high in the Midcontinent, and supplies in the (U.S.) Gulf will have no where to go because the Harbor doesn't need them," said John Bradberry, vice president at Transmontaigne Products Services Inc in Fayettville, Arkansas.
February gasoline ended off 1.71 cents a gallon at 70.48 cents, while the March contract ended at 70.63 cents.
Contango refers to the price of the nearer contract in time being less expensive than the proceeding contract.
"The big talk today was of the cargoes heading over. There was a lot of selling from February into March," said a New York gasoline dealer.
February crude ended 25 cents off at $26.37 a barrel, and February heating oil settled 0.38 cent down at 73.05 cents a gallon, with both caught under gasoline's downdraft.
Steve Platt, analyst with Dean Witter in Chicago, said gasoline could remain in contango in the short term since it is in a period of seasonally weak demand.
Crude's price may suffer in turn since it was supply tightness in refined products which helped stoke demand for crude in recent months, he said.
"It (gasoline's price) shows ample supply in the near term, but in the big picture it may mean something regarding the products' ability to support crude," said Platt.
Talk of the imports follows oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute Tuesday which showed gasoline stocks up a whopping 4.3 million barrels for the week ended January 3.
Reformulated gasoline stocks, which is the gasoline deliverable against the NYMEX contract, grew 2.8 million barrels in the New York Harbor region of the East Coast.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
